# Dhammadāyāda Sutta (MN 3 (PTS MN i 12))

**ID:** MN 3 (PTS MN i 12)
**Section:** Majjhimanikāya (mn)
**Collection:** Sutta
**Title (Pali):** Dhammadāyāda Sutta
**PTS:** MN i 12
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0201m.mul0.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Dhammadāyāda Sutta* (MN 3, PTS MN i 12) is the third discourse in the *Mūlapariyāyavagga* of the *Majjhimanikāya* [Ñāṇamoli & Bodhi 1995]. In this discourse, the Buddha exhorts the monks to become heirs in the Dhamma (the spiritual path of contentment) rather than heirs in material possessions [Ñāṇamoli & Bodhi 1995]. Venerable Sāriputta subsequently elaborates on this exhortation, explaining how disciples should emulate the Buddha's conduct and train themselves in order to experience the fruits of the path [Ñāṇamoli & Bodhi 1995].

Curated parallels to the sutta exist in the Chinese Āgamas, specifically in the *Madhyama-āgama* (MĀ 88) and the *Ekottarika-āgama* (EĀ 18.3), although early comparative studies initially marked it as unidentified [Anesaki 1908]. The sutta is also cited in post-canonical literature, notably in the *Milindapañha* (Mil 6.1.2).
